text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim reminds media to exercise greater discretion when publishing photographs of juvenile suspects.
-- Police seize 1.2 million ringgit in cash and property believed to have been purchased using money obtained from the sale of drugs.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says he did not expect any substantial change in the economic and foreign policies of China with the death of the country's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
-- Mahathir says has asked the Burmese government to help Malaysia deport 8,000 illegal Burmese immigrants.
-- Anwar says half the country's social problems can be resolved if parents take their responsibilities seriously.
-- Mahathir says the draft of the cyber laws for Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) is ready and will be tabled during next month's parliament sitting.
